sections.h2: Ways to sell a Converse house
sections.html:
Of the three usual routes, cash is quickest, and it fits a house needing work or a seller up against a firm date. Listing with an agent and selling on your own remain open.

Converse lies in northeastern Bexar County, roughly thirteen miles from downtown San Antonio, on Farm Road 1976. Some sellers are longtime owners. Others are heirs, or owners facing a tax bill or a transfer to another city.

  • Cash buyer: an as-is price, a closing day you pick and no showings.
  • Agent listing: more exposure, but showings, buyer loans and repair requests add weeks.
  • Inherited house: settle first which heir or executor has authority to sign.
  • Sale with taxes due: the payoff is taken out of your proceeds at closing.

This is a young, growing city where roughly three homes in four are owner-occupied. Households average 2.86 people, and 27.7% of residents are under 18, so family-size houses are the typical product. The city has 10,288 households and an average commute of 26.8 minutes.

Population rose from 8,887 in 1990 to 11,508 in 2000 and 32,481 today. Expect older homes near the original roads next to subdivisions that appeared after the 1990s. Tell buyers which kind yours is, because age drives their questions about roofs, plumbing and foundations.

sections.h2: When Bexar County property taxes are due
sections.html:
Statements arrive in October. Payment is due by January 31, and a postmark on or before that day counts as on time. An unpaid account is delinquent as of February 1.

On July 1, past-due accounts are handed to collectors and an extra 15 or 20 percent fee attaches. Business property accounts can be sent out as early as April 1.

  • Bexar Appraisal District sets values, grants exemptions and records changes of ownership or address.
  • The tax office mails bills and accepts payments, and will issue a duplicate if yours never shows up.
  • A lost bill excuses nothing, so the tax, penalty, interest and lien all stay in force.

Three plans exist, and your exemptions decide which you can join. A half-payment option splits the base tax between late November and the end of June. A four-payment plan is for homestead owners who are older or disabled. The ten-month plan runs October through July and is open to homestead owners with a disabled, over-65 or disabled veteran exemption, or a qualifying surviving spouse.

Bexar County is the only Texas county offering the ten-month plan, and it can still be joined in November with 20 percent down. Early-payment discounts ended under a 2003 commissioners court order, so there is no reward for paying ahead. A mailed payment is judged by its postmark, and a forgotten reminder does not extend a deadline.

sections.h2: Postponing taxes for older or military owners
sections.html:
Owners who are 65 or disabled may file a deferral affidavit with Bexar Appraisal District, and interest accrues at five percent a year. When the owner moves out or no longer owns the home, the back taxes and deferred interest come due on the 181st day.

Service members on active duty outside Texas during a declared war or emergency can defer under Property Tax Code section 31.02(b) by filing form 50-305 with their orders. If you hold a deferral, request a payoff figure before you list.

Order a tax certificate. It costs $10.00, payment comes first, and it shows the status of taxes, including penalties and interest if they are delinquent.

If you owned the house on January 1, you remain personally liable for that year's tax even after selling in July, and the lien stays attached to the property. Title agents and buyers therefore insist on the certificate before closing. Order yours early.

sections.h2: Exemptions that help a buyer or seller
sections.html:
Local exemptions include the general residence homestead, a disabled exemption, a 100 percent disabled veteran exemption and an over-65 exemption. For school taxes, $140,000 comes off a homestead, with $60,000 more at age 65 or for a disability.

Someone buying after January 1 can begin the exemption immediately when the seller never had one. File applications with the appraisal district before May 1.

sections.h2: An inherited house or one with liens
sections.html:
First prove who may sign the deed. Texas gives heirs four years to probate a will, offers a small estate affidavit for modest estates, and lets an owner pass a house without probate through a deed recorded during life. Title agents want one of those papers before they close.

Tax foreclosures carry their own rules. A homestead owner has two years after the purchaser's deed is filed to redeem, and the former owner can claim surplus from a tax foreclosure for two years.

Before you talk to buyers, gather the deed, a Bexar tax statement or certificate, each lender's payoff figure and proof of any exemption or deferral on the account. For an inherited house, add the will or court order and a list of heirs. A buyer's title agent will request all of it, and having it ready keeps the closing date from slipping.

Photos of repairs you have already made, and a plain list of ones you have not, help a cash buyer quote faster. They also help a listing agent describe the house honestly.

Offers differ in more than price. Ask each buyer whether the figure stays firm after the walkthrough, who pays for the title policy, how long the inspection window lasts and whether you may stay a few days after closing. Write the answers down, then compare offers by the amount you would take home and the number of weeks to funding.

sections.h2: How a cash sale moves along
sections.html:
You provide the address and describe the condition. The buyer visits, then makes an offer on paper that reflects any repairs. When you accept, a title company opens the file, searches for liens and tax balances and collects payoff letters. You choose the closing date, and funds reach you after the lender and the county have been paid.

Skipping a listing means skipping buyer loans and repair negotiations, which is where weeks usually disappear. In exchange, expect a price below a retail sale. Weigh the offer by what you would net after commission, repairs and the carrying costs of waiting.

faqs.a: In northeastern Bexar County, about thirteen miles northeast of downtown San Antonio, on Farm Road 1976.

faqs.q: Does Bexar County have a ten-month tax payment plan?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the only Texas county with one. It is open to homesteads with an over-65, disabled or disabled veteran exemption, or a qualifying surviving spouse.

faqs.q: What is a Bexar County tax certificate?
faqs.a: It is a document showing the status of taxes on a property, with penalties and interest if delinquent. The fee is $10.00 and payment comes first.

faqs.q: Who sets property values for a Converse home?
faqs.a: Bexar Appraisal District values the property and decides exemptions. The tax office bills and collects. Call the district about exemptions and the tax office about statements.

faqs.q: Do I still owe taxes if I sold my Converse house during the year?
faqs.a: The owner on January 1 stays personally liable, and the lien follows the property, so the closing papers should settle that year's tax.
